title: Density-aware controls, localized cost annunciation, and keyboard flow for rollout toasts
creator: Maya Ortiz
description: Improve accessibility and localization of the Console cost and rollout surfaces by introducing a density-aware control pattern, verbal/sr-friendly cost summaries for localized number formats, and a predictable keyboard flow for rollout toast interactions. This ticket bundles the design work, prototype, and initial review feedback for the engineering handoff.
background: Recent QA and customer reports highlighted two recurring issues: (1) localized large-number formats (eg. compact notation vs full) break screen reader summaries and produce inconsistent voiceover output for non-English locales; (2) rollout toasts plus compact density controls create focus loss for keyboard users when a toast appears during rapid toggling. We also want to reduce visual noise on cost dashboards with a density toggle that adapts spacing while preserving contrast and semantic order for assistive tech.
acceptance_criteria: Density toggle implemented with a11y-friendly labels and aria-live region that does not interrupt ongoing announcements
Screen-reader summary for selected cost window reads localized numbers correctly (examples provided) and includes units in the user locale
Toast appear/disappear does not steal focus; keyboard focus returns to invoking control and toasts are reachable via a consistent tab stop (or explicit 'Show latest toast' control)
High-contrast mode maps use tokenized color variables; contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for text and >= 3:1 for UI components per our visual design tokens
Design spec includes edge-case flows for RTL locales and number formatting where compact notation differs (e.g., '1,2M' vs '1.2M')
accessibility_findings: Screen-reader currently announces compact numbers verbatim (e.g., '1.2M') without localized unit expansion
Density toggle lacks an accessible label and aria-pressed semantics; keyboard users lose context when layout snaps
Rollout toast appears with aria-live=polite but gains DOM focus unexpectedly in Safari/VO leading to navigation break
Some cost table header cells rely on color only to indicate 'estimated' vs 'actual' which fails contrast and semantic cues
i18n_findings: Compact number formatting differs per locale — some locales use narrow no-break spaces and different decimal separators
Currency and unit placement varies; speaking 'USD' vs local symbol causes ambiguity in voice-only summaries
RTL layouts invert controls; current toast placement overlaps the keyboard focus ring in several edge cases
decisions: Use aria-live region with role='status' for non-interruptive cost summaries and reserve aria-atomic for full reannounce only when window changes substantially
Density toggle will expose 'dense' | 'comfortable' states with aria-pressed on a segmented control and explicit visually-hidden labels for screen readers
Rollout toasts will not take autofocus; instead add a persistent 'Last notification' toolbar button to jump to the most recent toast for keyboard/sr users
Number-to-speech rules will expand compact notation to full localized phrases in SR mode (e.g., '1.2M' -> '1.2 million' in English, locale-specific expansion for others)
tasks: Finalize Figma states for dense/comfortable with high-contrast token overlays
Create ARIA spec snippet and example code for engineering (aria-live, role=status, aria-pressed patterns)
Produce a localization test matrix with examples for en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ar-SA, and pt-BR
Work with i18n eng to add speech expansion helpers into shared i18n library
Dev QA session scheduled: a11y group + i18n reviewer + keyboard-only walkthrough
review_comments: PM (Arjun Patel): ensure 'Last notification' button is discoverable within Console toolbar and doesn't conflict with existing keyboard shortcuts
Eng (Samir Shah): we should avoid heavy JS localization at render-time; propose server-side pre-expanded announcements for large dashboards
A11y reviewer (Priya Choudhary): prefer role='status' over aria-live=polite on dynamic summary because it behaves more consistently across NVDA/JAWS
i18n reviewer (Elena Garcia): confirm examples for locales where compact suffixes are alphabetic rather than metric-style (eg. 'k' vs local abbreviations)
next_steps: Address review feedback in prototype and re-run keyboard/screen reader scenarios (owner: Linh Nguyen)
Sync with Eng on implementation approach and finalize PR reference; tag ENG-19812 as implementation epic
Add localization test cases to CI harness and schedule bilingual QA session with fr-FR and ja-JP speakers
Document the 'Last notification' keyboard shortcut and accessibility notes in the Console Help center
